page: Microsoft Azure F64als_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine built on dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 hardware operating at clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz. The instance delivers 64 physical cores mapped to 64 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading, ensuring predictable execution without thread-sharing overhead. System memory is sized at 128.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cache provisions include 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache. Modern vector and cryptographic execution extensions are fully enabled, including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, AVX-VNNI, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark measurements place the F64als_v7 in the top tier for raw integer, cryptographic, and floating-point throughput. Synthetic tests via stress-ng demonstrate top-decile ratings in both single-threaded (3,787.98) and multi-threaded (233,270.61) compute runs. Memory throughput performance is similarly elevated, registering uncached read speeds of 410.03 GB/sec and uncached write speeds of 205.23 GB/sec. Data processing tests show rapid throughput, reaching 869.45 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and 171.03 million operations per second in Redis SET operations. For machine learning inference, prompt processing throughput on 7B parameter models remains in the top 10% tier at 316.09 tokens per second.

A key architectural consideration is the complete absence of local disk storage and complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Persistent operating system and data volumes must be provisioned via remote block storage. While the 2.0 GB per core memory profile is unsuitable for vast memory-resident data sets, it yields high compute density per allocated dollar. The F64als_v7 is particularly effective for compute-bound pipelines such as distributed compilation, batch video encoding, scientific simulations, cryptographic workloads, and small-to-medium parameter CPU-based inference tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure F64als_v7 is a compute-optimized instance powered by a 64-core AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz, paired with 128 GB of RAM. Configured with a dedicated 1:1 vCPU-to-physical-core architecture and 2.0 GB of memory per core, it eliminates multi-threading contention for deterministic computational throughput. The processor supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, and SHA-NI, which deliver top-tier benchmark results across vector calculations, compression algorithms, and cryptographic operations. The instance lacks bundled local storage and complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating external disk attachments for persistent state. Memory bandwidth reaches over 410 GB/sec for uncached read operations, facilitating high-rate data manipulation and high-throughput static web serving. While less suited for large in-memory databases due to its 1:2 memory ratio, the F64als_v7 delivers high compute density and cost efficiency for continuous batch workloads, video encoding, engineering simulations, and moderate-parameter LLM inference.
